sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x)=x-1 \\ f(f(x))=f(x)-1=x-1-1=x-2 \\ g(f(f(x)))=e^{x-2} \\ \therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{-2\sqrt{x}}\times e^{x-2}-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}y \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}y=e^{x-2\sqrt{x}-2}\text{which is L.D.E} \\ \text{I.F.}=e^{\int \frac{dy}{\sqrt{x}}}=e^{2\sqrt{x}} \end{array}$

Its solution is

$\begin{array}{l} y\times e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\int e^{2\sqrt{x}}\times e^{x-2\sqrt{x}-2}dx+c \\ y\times e^{2\sqrt{x}}=\int e^{x-2}dx+c \\ y\times e^{2\sqrt{x}}=e^{x-2}+c \end{array}$

Given $\mathrm{x}=0,\mathrm{y}=0\Rightarrow 0=\mathrm{e}^{-2}+\mathrm{c};\mathrm{c}=-\mathrm{e}^{-2}$

$\therefore \mathrm{y}\times \mathrm{e}^{2\sqrt{x}}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}-2}-\mathrm{e}^{-2}$

when $\mathrm{x}=1,\mathrm{y}\times \mathrm{e}^{2}=\mathrm{e}^{-1}-\mathrm{e}^{-2}$

$y=\frac{e^{-1}-e^{-2}}{e^{2}}=\frac{\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{e2}}{e^{2}}=\frac{e^{2}-e}{e^{5}}=\frac{e-1}{e^{4}}$

Option (2) is correct

text: Let $a$ be the length of a side of a square OABC with O being the origin. Its side OA makes an acute angle $α$ with the positive x-axis and the equations of its diagonals are $(\sqrt{3}+1)x+(\sqrt{3}-1)y=0$ and $(\sqrt{3}-1)x-(\sqrt{3}+1)y+8\sqrt{3}=0$. Then $a^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
The diagonal $(\sqrt{3}+1)x+(\sqrt{3}-1)y=0$ passes through $O$, so it is $OB$, and $AC$ is $(\sqrt{3}-1)x-(\sqrt{3}+1)y+8\sqrt{3}=0$.

The diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles, so the distance of $O$ from $AC$ is half the diagonal $OB$, that is $\dfrac{a\sqrt{2}}{2}=\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$.

$\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{(\sqrt{3}-1)^{2}+(\sqrt{3}+1)^{2}}}=\dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8}}=2\sqrt{6}$

$a=2\sqrt{12}=4\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow a^{2}=48$

The slope of $OB$ is $-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}=-(2+\sqrt{3})=\tan 105^{\circ }$, and $OA$ makes $45^{\circ }$ with $OB$, so the acute angle is $α=105^{\circ }-45^{\circ }=60^{\circ }$; the side length does not depend on it.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: Let $α$ be a solution of $x^{2}+x+1=0$, and for some a and b in $\mathrm{ℝ}$, $[\begin{array}{lll} 4 & a & b \end{array}]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 16 & 13 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & -14 & -8 \end{array}\right ]=[\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}]$. If $\frac{4}{α^{4}}+\frac{m}{α^{a}}+\frac{n}{α^{b}}=3$, then m + n is equal to $_______$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $α$ be a solution of the equation $x^{2}+x+1=0$. This implies that $α$ is a cube root of unity, denoted as $ω$, where $α^{2}+α+1=0$.

We are given matrix equations with parameters $a$ and $b$ as follows:

$[\begin{array}{lll} 4 & a & b \end{array}]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 16 & 13 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & -14 & -8 \end{array}\right ]=[\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}]$

Solving these equations:

$\begin{array}{l} [4-a-2b,64-a-14b,52+2a-8b]=[0,0,0] \\ \Rightarrow a+2b=4 \\ \Rightarrow a+14b=64 \end{array}$

From these, solve for $a$ and $b$:

$\begin{array}{l} 12b=60\Rightarrow b=5 \\ a=-6 \end{array}$

We now substitute $a$ and $b$ into the given function:

$\frac{4}{α^{4}}+\frac{m}{α^{a}}+\frac{n}{α^{b}}=3$

We substitute $α=ω$ and simplify:

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{4}{ω}+\dfrac{m}{1}+\dfrac{n}{ω^{2}}=3 \\ \Rightarrow 4ω^{2}+m+nω=3 \end{array}$

Substitute $ω=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$ and $ω^{2}=-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i$:

$\begin{array}{l} 4\left (-\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right )+m+n\left (-\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right )=3 \\ \Rightarrow -2+m-\dfrac{n}{2}=3 \\ \text{and}\dfrac{-4\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{n\sqrt{3}}{2}=0 \end{array}$

From the above, solve for $n$ and $m$:

$\begin{array}{l} n=4 \\ m=7 \end{array}$

Thus, $m+n=11$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: The value of $\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{1+\tan ^{2}(2)}-1}{\tan (2)}\right )-\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{1+\tan ^{2}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}+1}{\tan \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\sqrt{1+\tan ^{2}θ}=|\sec θ|$, the expression is

$\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{|\sec 2|-1}{\tan 2}\right )-\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\left |\sec \frac{1}{2}\right |+1}{\tan \frac{1}{2}}\right )$

As $\dfrac{π}{2}<2<π$, $\cos 2<0$, so $|\sec 2|=-\sec 2$ and

$\frac{-\sec 2-1}{\tan 2}=\frac{-1-\cos 2}{\sin 2}=-\frac{2\cos ^{2}1}{2\sin 1\cos 1}=-\cot 1$

As $0<\dfrac{1}{2}<\dfrac{π}{2}$, $\left |\sec \frac{1}{2}\right |=\sec \frac{1}{2}$ and

$\frac{\sec \frac{1}{2}+1}{\tan \frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1+\cos \frac{1}{2}}{\sin \frac{1}{2}}=\frac{2\cos ^{2}\frac{1}{4}}{2\sin \frac{1}{4}\cos \frac{1}{4}}=\cot \frac{1}{4}$

Using $\cot ^{-1}(-y)=π-\cot ^{-1}y$, and $1,\dfrac{1}{4}\in (0,π)$:

$\cot ^{-1}(-\cot 1)-\cot ^{-1}\left (\cot \frac{1}{4}\right )=(π-1)-\frac{1}{4}=π-\frac{5}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{\tan ^{-1}x+\log _{e}\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}-2x}{x^{5}}\right )=\frac{2}{5}$

Statement II: $\lim _{x\to 1}\left (x^{\frac{2}{1-x}}\right )=\frac{1}{e^{2}}$

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\log _{e}\sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}=\dfrac{1}{2}[\ln (1+x)-\ln (1-x)]$ and $\ln (1\pm x)=\pm x-\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\pm \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}-\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}\pm \dfrac{x^{5}}{5}-\ldots$, the even powers cancel:

$\log _{e}\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}=x+\frac{x^{3}}{3}+\frac{x^{5}}{5}+\ldots$

The series of the inverse tangent is $\tan ^{-1}x=x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}+\dfrac{x^{5}}{5}-\ldots$

Adding the two series and subtracting $2x$, the $x$ and $x^{3}$ terms cancel:

$\tan ^{-1}x+\log _{e}\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}-2x=\frac{2x^{5}}{5}+O(x^{7}),$

so the limit in Statement I is $\dfrac{2}{5}$ and Statement I is true.

Statement II is of the form $1^{\infty }$:

$\lim _{x\to 1}x^{\frac{2}{1-x}}=e^{\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{2}{1-x}(x-1)}=e^{-2}=\frac{1}{e^{2}},$

so Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: The integral $\int\limits _{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}}\left (|π^{2}x\sin (πx)\left |)dx \right.  \right.$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $|π^{2}x\sin πx|=π^{2}|x\sin πx|$, the sign of $x\sin πx$ decides the split. On $[-1,0]$ both $x$ and $\sin πx$ are $\leq 0$, and on $[0,1]$ both are $\geq 0$, so $x\sin πx\geq 0$ on $[-1,1]$. On $\left [1,\frac{3}{2}\right ]$, $x>0$ and $\sin πx\leq 0$, so $x\sin πx\leq 0$ there.

As $x\sin πx$ is even,

$I=π^{2}\left [\int\limits _{-1}^{1}x\sin πxdx-\int\limits _{1}^{3/2}x\sin πxdx\right ]=π^{2}\left [2\int\limits _{0}^{1}x\sin πxdx-\int\limits _{1}^{3/2}x\sin πxdx\right ]$

By parts, $F(x)=\int x\sin πxdx=-\dfrac{x\cos πx}{π}+\dfrac{\sin πx}{π^{2}}$, with $F(0)=0$, $F(1)=\dfrac{1}{π}$ and $F\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )=-\dfrac{1}{π^{2}}$.

$I=π^{2}\left [\dfrac{2}{π}-\left (-\dfrac{1}{π^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{π}\right )\right ]=π^{2}\left [\dfrac{3}{π}+\dfrac{1}{π^{2}}\right ]=3π+1$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text:
Let A = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Let R be a relation on A defined by (x, y) ∈ R if and only if max{x, y} ∈ {3, 4}. Then among the statements
 $(S_{1})$: The number of elements in R is 18, and
 $(S_{2})$: The relation R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To evaluate the relation $R$ on the set $A=\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$, we first need to understand the conditions for an element $(x,y)$ to be in $R$. Specifically, $(x,y)\in R$ if and only if $\max \{x,y\}\in \{3,4\}$.

Considering this, let's list the pairs:

For $\max \{x,y\}=3$, the possible pairs are:

$(0,3),(3,0),(1,3),(3,1),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3)$

For $\max \{x,y\}=4$, the possible pairs are:

$(0,4),(4,0),(1,4),(4,1),(2,4),(4,2),(3,4),(4,3),(4,4)$

Combining these, the set $R$ consists of the following elements:

$R=\{(0,3),(3,0),(1,3),(3,1),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(0,4),(4,0),(1,4),(4,1),(2,4),(4,2),(3,4),(4,3),(4,4)\}$

This gives us a total of 16 elements in $R$, not 18 as initially claimed in statement $S_{1}$.

Next, we analyze the properties of the relation $R$:

Reflexivity: A relation is reflexive if $(x,x)\in R$ for all $x\in A$. For example, $(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)$ are not in $R$, so $R$ is not reflexive.

Symmetry: A relation is symmetric if whenever $(a,b)\in R$, then $(b,a)\in R$ as well. For all pairs $(x,y)$ listed, both $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ are present. Thus, $R$ is symmetric.

Transitivity: A relation is transitive if whenever $(a,b)\in R$ and $(b,c)\in R$, then $(a,c)\in R$. An example where transitivity fails is $(0,3)$ and $(3,1)$ are in $R$ but $(0,1)$ is not in $R$. Therefore, $R$ is not transitive.

In conclusion, statement $S_{2}$ is correct as $R$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: Let f(x) be a positive function and $I_{1}=\int\limits _{-\frac{1}{2}}^{1}2xf(2x(1-2x))dx$ and $I_{2}=\int\limits _{-1}^{2}f(x(1-x))dx$. Then the value of $\frac{I_{2}}{I_{1}}$ is equal to $________$

solution.body:
In $I_{1}=\int\limits _{-1/2}^{1}2xf\left (2x(1-2x)\right )dx$, put $2x=t$, so $dx=\dfrac{dt}{2}$ and the limits become $-1$ and $2$:

$I_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{-1}^{2}tf\left (t(1-t)\right )dt$

Replacing $t$ by $(-1+2)-t=1-t$ leaves $t(1-t)$ unchanged, so

$\int\limits _{-1}^{2}tf\left (t(1-t)\right )dt=\int\limits _{-1}^{2}(1-t)f\left (t(1-t)\right )dt$

Adding the two forms, $2\int\limits _{-1}^{2}tf\left (t(1-t)\right )dt=\int\limits _{-1}^{2}f\left (t(1-t)\right )dt=I_{2}$.

So $I_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{I_{2}}{2}=\dfrac{I_{2}}{4}$, and since $f>0$ gives $I_{2}>0$, $\dfrac{I_{2}}{I_{1}}=4$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

text: There are 12 points in a plane, no three of which are in the same straight line, except 5 points which are collinear. Then the total number of triangles that can be formed with the vertices at any three of these 12 points is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To count the number of distinct triangles:

Start with all possible triples of points.  

From 12 points, the number of ways to choose any 3 is  

$\left (12 3\right )=\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1}=220.$

Subtract the “invalid” triples that are collinear.  

The only collinear sets of three points arise from the single line containing the 5 collinear points.  

Number of ways to pick 3 points from those 5 is  

$\left (5 3\right )=10.$

Valid triangles = total triples − collinear triples.  

$220-10=210.$

Hence, the total number of triangles that can be formed is 210.

Correct option: B

text: If A and B are two events such that $P(A)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.4$ and $P(A\cap B–)=0.5$, where $B–$ denotes the complement of B, then $P\left (B|(A\cup B–)\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $P(A)=0.7$, $P(B)=0.4$ and $P(A\cap B–)=0.5$, so $P(B–)=1-0.4=0.6$.

$P(A\cap B)=P(A)-P(A\cap B–)=0.7-0.5=0.2$

$P(A\cup B–)=P(A)+P(B–)-P(A\cap B–)=0.7+0.6-0.5=0.8$

Since $B\cap B–=\emptyset$, $B\cap (A\cup B–)=(B\cap A)\cup (B\cap B–)=A\cap B$.

$P\left (B|A\cup B–\right )=\dfrac{P\left (B\cap (A\cup B–)\right )}{P(A\cup B–)}=\dfrac{0.2}{0.8}=\dfrac{1}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift

$\begin{array}{l} A=\text{Required Area}=\left [\int\limits _{0}^{1}(-3\sqrt{x})dx-\int\limits _{0}^{1}(3x-6)dx\right ] \\ A=-3\left (\dfrac{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}\right )\left |_{0}^{1}-\left (\dfrac{3x^{2}}{2}-6x\right )\right |_{0}^{1} \\ A=-2[1-0]\left [\dfrac{3}{2}-6\right ] \\ A=-2-\dfrac{3}{2}+6=\dfrac{5}{2}\text{Sq. unit} \\ \therefore 6A=6\times \dfrac{5}{2}=15 \end{array}$

text: Let $r$ be the radius of the circle, which touches $x$ - axis at point $(a,0),a<0$ and the parabola $\mathrm{y}^{2}=9x$ at the point $(4,6)$. Then $r$ is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} (x-a)^{2}+(y-r)^{2}=r^{2} \\ (4-a)^{2}+(6-r)^{2}=r^{2} \\ 16+a^{2}-8a+36+r^{2}-12r=r^{2} \\ a^{2}-8a-12r+52=0 \end{array}$

Tangent to parabola at $(4,6)$ is

$6y=9\cdot \left (\frac{x+4}{2}\right )\text{i.e.}3x-4y+12=0$

This is also tangent to the circle

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad CP=r \\ \dfrac{3a-4r+12}{5}=\pm r \end{array}$

$3\mathrm{a}+12=4\mathrm{r}\pm 5\mathrm{r}\left \{\begin{array}{l} 9\mathrm{r} \\ -\mathrm{r} \end{array}\text{..... (1)} \right.$

equation of circle is

$(x-a)^{2}+(y-r)^{2}=r^{2}$

satisfy $P(4,6)\Rightarrow a^{2}-8a-12r+52=0\text{..... (2)}$

From equation (1)

If $\mathrm{a}+4=3\mathrm{r}$ then $\mathrm{a}=+6$ (rejected)

If $3a+12=-r$ then $a=-14$ and $r=30$

text: Let the area of the triangle formed by the lines $x+2=y-1=z,\frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y}{-1}=\frac{z-1}{1}$ and $\frac{x}{-3}=\frac{y-3}{3}=\frac{z-2}{1}$ be $A$. Then $A^{2}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 8th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In parametric form, $L_{1}$: $(t-2,t+1,t)$, $L_{2}$: $(5m+3,-m,m+1)$ and $L_{3}$: $(-3n,3n+3,n+2)$.

$L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$: $t+1=-m$ and $t=m+1$ give $m=-1$, $t=0$; the $x$-coordinates agree ($-2=-5+3$), so the vertex is $P(-2,1,0)$.

$L_{2}$ and $L_{3}$: $m+1=n+2$ and $-m=3n+3$ give $n=-1$, $m=0$; the $x$-coordinates agree ($3=3$), so the vertex is $Q(3,0,1)$.

$L_{3}$ and $L_{1}$: $n+2=t$ and $-3n=t-2$ give $n=0$, $t=2$; the $y$-coordinates agree ($3=3$), so the vertex is $R(0,3,2)$.

$QP\leftarrow =(-5,1,-1)$ and $QR\leftarrow =(-3,3,1)$, so

$QP\leftarrow \times QR\leftarrow =\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -5 & 1 & -1 \\ -3 & 3 & 1 \end{array}\right |=4\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-12\hat{k}$

$A=\dfrac{1}{2}\left |QP\leftarrow \times QR\leftarrow \right |=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{16+64+144}=\dfrac{\sqrt{224}}{2}$

$A^{2}=\dfrac{224}{4}=56$

Hence, the answer is 56.

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x)=\cos ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow -1\leq \left (\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\right )\leq 1 \\ \left (\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\right )\geq -1 \\ \dfrac{4x+5+3x-7}{3x-7}\geq 0 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{7x-2}{3x-7}\geq 0 \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} x\in \left (-\infty ,\dfrac{2}{7}\right ]\cup \left (\dfrac{7}{3},\infty \right ) \\ &\dfrac{4x+5}{3x-7}\leq 1\Rightarrow \dfrac{x+12}{3x-7}\leq 0 \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\therefore$ Domain of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is

$\left [-12,\frac{2}{7}\right ]α=-12,β=\frac{2}{7}$

$g(x)=\log _{2}(2-6\log _{27}(2x+5))$

Domain

$2-6\log _{27}(2x+5)>0$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 6\log _{27}(2\mathrm{x}+5)<2 \\ \Rightarrow  & \log _{27}(2\mathrm{x}+5)<\frac{1}{3} \\ \Rightarrow  & 2\mathrm{x}+5<3 \\ \Rightarrow  & \mathrm{x}<-1 \end{array}$

$&2x+5>0\Rightarrow x>-\frac{5}{2}$

Domain is $\mathrm{x}\in \left (-\frac{5}{2},-1\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} γ=-\dfrac{5}{2},δ=-1 \\ \begin{array}{l} |7(α+β)+4(γ+δ)|=\left |7\left (-12+\dfrac{2}{7}\right )+4\left (-\dfrac{5}{2}-1\right )\right | \\ |-82-14|=96 \end{array} \end{array}$
